system.name: RingLeader
system.one_liner: a system that offloads intra-server request scheduling and load balancing across services and cores to the NIC

components.name: On-NIC Storage
components.role: NIC-side storage container holding per-service scheduling and queuing state

components.name: SRAM (Cache)
components.role: fast cache tier for hot per-service queue data

components.name: Per-Service Scheduling and Queuing
components.role: per-service queue structures holding buffered requests

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: on-NIC scheduler component implementing the FEO discipline

components.name: Queue Manager
components.role: manages enqueue and dequeue of queue descriptors for FEO

components.name: FEO
components.role: first-eligible-out priority queue that evaluates each element's eligibility via a bitmask and dequeues the highest-priority eligible element

components.name: Load Balancer
components.role: supplies the eligibility bitmask to FEO and issues read requests to fetch data for the dispatched request

flows.what: Eligibility Mask used to Eval eligibility

content.key_idea: FEO extends a PIFO priority queue by filtering elements to only those eligible for dispatch, via a bitmask supplied by the load balancer, before scheduling the smallest-ranked eligible element, avoiding head-of-line blocking.
content.reading_order: Top-down then left-right: requests stored in On-NIC Storage (DRAM/SRAM per-service queues) are enqueued as descriptors into the Scheduler's Queue Manager and FEO, which evaluates eligibility against a bitmask from the Load Balancer before dequeuing back to it; the Load Balancer issues Read Requests back to storage.

evidence: As Figure 6 shows, when dequeuing elements, we first filter the set of elements eligible for dispatch
the load balancer provides a bitmask that records the dispatching eligibility of each service
FEO uses priority encoding to select the front-most element whose eligibility is true

summary: This figure zooms into RingLeader's on-NIC request scheduler, detailing the First-Eligible-Out (FEO) priority queue introduced to avoid head-of-line blocking. On-NIC Storage (DRAM for bulk storage, SRAM as cache) holds per-service scheduling and queuing state and issues a Store Request into the Scheduler's Queue Manager, which enqueues a queue descriptor into FEO. The Load Balancer supplies an Eligibility Mask (shown as an example 1-1-1-0 bit pattern) that FEO evaluates in parallel against each queued element; FEO then uses priority encoding to dequeue the front-most eligible element as a queue descriptor back to the Load Balancer, which issues a Read Request back to On-NIC Storage to fetch the corresponding data. Boxes are flat-filled: blue for On-NIC Storage, orange for the Scheduler/Queue Manager/Load Balancer, with green-shaded squares marking occupied or eligible queue slots.
